# FDG6021

> DO NOT declare protected or virtual members on sealed types.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 6.3 Sealing.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Not checked: the C# compiler reports a new protected member of a sealed type (warning CS0628, protected internal and private protected included) and rejects a new virtual member of a sealed type (error CS0549), a protected member of a struct (error CS0666) and a protected member of a static class (error CS1057); a probe with SDK 10.0.402 showed this for sealed classes and sealed records. Overrides, which the compiler allows, declare no new protected or virtual member.

## From the book

By definition, sealed types cannot be inherited from. This means that protected members on sealed types cannot be called, and virtual methods on sealed types cannot be overridden.
